author: Pellam Goodbarrel, innkeeper and historian of small things
pages:
#How It Began

In the village of Bramblemoor there were two cheesemakers, the widow Astrid and old Gunnar, and between them there was a single hill. Each believed the hill belonged to them, because each of their goats grazed upon it, and goats, as everyone knows, are excellent judges of property law.

#The First Wheel

One morning a wheel of cheese rolled down the hill and through Astrid's front door. It bore Gunnar's mark. Astrid, who was not a forgiving woman, rolled it back up the hill with a strongly worded note pinned to the rind.

Gunnar, who was not a reading man, assumed the note was a compliment and rolled down two wheels in gratitude.

#Escalation

By the end of the month, cheese wheels were rolling down that hill in both directions at all hours. Travellers learned to cross Bramblemoor at a run. The village guard, a nervous young man named Tolvar the Lesser, was knocked flat four times in a single week and began wearing his shield on his back.

The local bandits, having heard rumours of a village where cheese literally fell from the sky, attempted to raid it and were defeated without anyone noticing they had been there.

#The Jarl Intervenes

At last the jarl sent her steward to settle the matter. The steward climbed the hill, stood at its very top, and declared that the hill belonged to neither cheesemaker but to the goats.

There was a terrible silence. Then both cheesemakers burst out laughing, because the goats had been eating the steward's cloak the entire time he was speaking.

#The Peace of Bramblemoor

Astrid and Gunnar now make cheese together, under a single mark: two goats butting heads. Their wheels are famous across the hold. Every year on the anniversary of the dispute, the village rolls a giant wheel down the hill, and whoever catches it is crowned Cheese Warden for the year.

Tolvar the Lesser has caught it six times. Nobody is quite sure whether he is very brave or simply very slow to get out of the way.
